shortSummary: Beloved autumn night-bloomer bearing snow-white pinwheel petals anchored by bright coral-orange tubular throats that carpet lawns at dawn.
leadOverview: Night-Flowering Jasmine (Nyctanthes arbor-tristis)—the poetic Shiuli or Shefali of Bengal—is a fragrant large shrub or small tree famous for opening its stars strictly after dusk and shedding them gently onto dewy grass before sunrise. Its botanical Latin name literally means 'Night Flower, Tree of Sadness', reflecting its nocturnal rhythm and bittersweet dawn carpet during Shorot autumn.

sections.title: Morphological Description
sections.subtitle: Quadrangular rough twigs, sandpaper leaves, coral-tubed blossoms, and flat heart capsules
sections.summary: Anatomy of four-angled stems, rough scabrous foliage, nocturnal salverform flowers, and papery bilobed capsules.
paragraphs: Nyctanthes arbor-tristis grows into a spreading shrub or small crooked tree 4 to 10 metres high with pale flaky bark and distinctive four-angled (quadrangular), stiffly hairy twigs. Opposite simple ovate leaves (6–12 cm long) feel noticeably rough like fine sandpaper on the upper surface due to silicified cystolith hairs, earning traditional folk utility for polishing fine wood.

From August through November, terminal trichotomous cymes open fragrant salverform flowers after sunset: 5 to 8 pure snow-white twisting pinwheel petals radiating from a striking cylindrical coral-orange corolla tube filled with nyctanthin carotenoid dye. At daybreak, petals cleanly detach intact, followed later by flat brown heart-shaped two-seeded capsules.

subblocks.heading: Quadrangular Stems
subblocks.text: Square young shoots and pale greyish peeling bark supporting an airy, multi-stemmed arching canopy up to 10 m.

subblocks.heading: Sandpaper Scabrous Leaves
subblocks.text: Opposite dark-green ovate leaves covered in rigid silica-rich trichomes that impart a gritty tactile texture.

subblocks.heading: Coral-Tubed Blossoms
subblocks.text: Nocturnal white 5–8-lobed pinwheel flowers anchored by vibrant orange-scarlet tubes brimming with nyctanthin pigment.

subblocks.heading: Compressed Heart Capsules
subblocks.text: Flat obcordate leathery green-to-brown bilocular seed pods (2 cm wide) splitting neatly down the center seam in winter.

sections.title: Taxonomy & Botanical Classification
sections.subtitle: Oleaceae olive-and-jasmine kinship despite square stems
sections.summary: Why Nyctanthes belongs to Oleaceae rather than Verbenaceae or nightshades.
paragraphs: Despite having square stems reminiscent of Lamiaceae or Verbenaceae, molecular phylogenetics and floral anatomy (two stamens fused inside a regular corolla tube and superior two-chambered ovary) confirm Nyctanthes arbor-tristis firmly inside family Oleaceae, order Lamiales—making Shiuli a cousin of Beli jasmine (Jasminum sambac) and olives.
Only two species form genus Nyctanthes worldwide, with arbor-tristis serving as the sole widely cherished garden species across South Asia.

sections.title: Natural Habitat & Global Distribution
sections.subtitle: Sub-Himalayan rocky hillsides to Bengali Shorot courtyards
sections.summary: Native across northern India and Nepal; naturalized in every sunlit South Asian homestead.
paragraphs: Wild Nyctanthes arbor-tristis inhabits dry rocky sub-Himalayan hills and moist deciduous forest edges from Kashmir, Nepal, and Assam southward into central India and Myanmar up to 1,500 metres elevation.

Across Bangladesh and West Bengal, Shiuli is an indispensable homestead guardian planted beside front gates and courtyard corners—awakening into snow-white autumn splendor beneath crisp blue Bhadro–Ashwin skies.

sections.title: Ecological Role & Pollinator Interactions
sections.subtitle: Sphingid hawkmoth night pollination and morning ant-scavenger recycling
sections.summary: Crepuscular scent peak for moths and rapid dawn abscission ecology.
paragraphs: At twilight, warm floral nectaries inside the narrow orange tube release sweet honey-musk volatiles (methyl anthranilate and phenylacetaldehyde) tailored to long-tongued nocturnal hawk moths (Sphingidae) and night-flying noctuid moths.
Once dawn sunlight rises, hormonal abscission cleanly drops spent corollas within hours—feeding ground ants and recycling moisture cleanly while conserving energy for the next evening's floral flush.

sections.title: Economic, Culinary & Cultural Importance
sections.subtitle: Icon of Shorot Durga Puja, morning garlands, and Buddhist saffron robes
sections.summary: Sacred flower gathering, Tagore literature, and non-toxic coral-orange natural dye.
paragraphs: Nothing captures Bengali autumn nostalgia like children barefoot at dawn gathering fragrant Shiuli blossoms from dewy grass in woven cane baskets ('Saji') for Durga Puja offerings, garlands, and Rabindra Sangeet poetry.

Crucially, dried coral-orange flower tubes yield 'nyctanthin'—an intense, water-soluble saffron carotenoid dye chemically identical to crocetin in true saffron—historically steeped to dye Buddhist monastic robes, fine silk saris, and natural culinary sweets.

sections.title: Traditional & Scientific Medicinal Properties
sections.subtitle: Arbortristoside iridoids, sciatica decoctions, and bitter leaf tonics
sections.summary: Ayurvedic 'Parijat' leaf infusions studied for antipyretic and anti-inflammatory activity.
paragraphs: Revered in Ayurveda as 'Parijat' or 'Harsingar', bitter fresh Shiuli leaves steeped in warm water or boiled slowly with black pepper are widely used across rural households for seasonal mild fever relief, stubborn sciatica joint discomfort, and sluggish digestion.

Phytochemical investigations isolate iridoid glycosides (arbortristosides A, B, and C), beta-sitosterol, oleanolic acid, and nyctanthic acid demonstrating antipyretic, anti-inflammatory, and hepatoprotective activity in preclinical assays.
sections.safetyNote: Nyctanthes leaves taste intensely bitter and may cause mild nausea or gastric irritation if brewed overly strong on an empty stomach; reserve medicinal leaf decoctions for short-term guidance and avoid concentrated extracts during pregnancy.

sections.title: Comprehensive Cultivation & Care Guide
sections.subtitle: Post-bloom winter pruning, seed or layering propagation, and full sun
sections.summary: Maintaining compact bushy flowering shrubs in pH 5.8–7.5 well-drained loam.
paragraphs: Propagate easily by sowing flat brown winter seeds soaked overnight or via monsoon semi-hardwood stem cuttings and air-layering. Grow plants in well-drained fertile loam (pH 5.8–7.5) receiving at least 6 hours of bright sunlight; excessive deep shade leads to leggy canes and sparse flowers.

Because Shiuli blooms profusely on fresh current-season growth, prune back elongated old limbs by one-third immediately after fruiting in late winter (February–March)—resulting in a tidy, multi-branched shrub bursting with thousands of blossoms every autumn.

sections.title: Annual Phenology & Six-Season Rhythms
sections.subtitle: Flowering, fruiting, vegetative flush, and Shororitu synchrony
sections.summary: Seasonal cadence across Bengal's six-season cycle (Autumn (শরৎ), Late Autumn (হেমন্ত)).
paragraphs: Night-Flowering Jasmine (Shiuli) (Nyctanthes arbor-tristis) aligns its vegetative flushes, anthesis, and fruit maturation tightly with Bengal's Shororitu photoperiod and monsoon moisture transitions, showing peak biological activity during Autumn (শরৎ), Late Autumn (হেমন্ত).

Autumn (শরৎ): Quintessential Shorot bloomer perfuming moonlit nights and carpeting dewy grass with coral-tubed white stars at dawn. Late Autumn (হেমন্ত): Final autumn blossom waves transition into flat heart-shaped green bilocular seed capsules.

subblocks.text: Synchronized with daylength shifts, pre-monsoon thermal buildup, and seasonal soil moisture oscillations.

sections.title: Seed Germination Biology & Propagation
sections.subtitle: Dormancy regulation, nursery media, and clonal propagation
sections.summary: Reproductive biology and reliable seed or vegetative propagation techniques for Night-Flowering Jasmine (Shiuli).
paragraphs: Night-Flowering Jasmine (Shiuli) (Nyctanthes arbor-tristis) combines sexual seed propagation—useful for raising sturdy heterozygous rootstocks—with elite clonal techniques such as veneer grafting, air layering (gootee), and semi-hardwood stem cuttings. Fresh recalcitrant or semi-orthodox seeds typically germinate within 14 to 35 days when depulped and sown in warm organic loam.
Clonal orchards standardize crown architecture, early precocity, and uniform biochemical profiles across generations within Oleaceae.

subblocks.heading: Nursery Seed Protocol
subblocks.text: Depulped seed sown cleanly in 2:1 loam-compost media; high viability when fresh.

subblocks.heading: Clonal Method
subblocks.text: Approach/veneer grafting or monsoon air-layering onto vigorous local rootstocks.

sections.title: Pathology Defense, Vectors & Organic IPM
sections.subtitle: Phytoalexin resilience, fungal prophylaxis, and predator guilds
sections.summary: Biochemical defense mechanisms and low-impact organic IPM guidelines for Nyctanthes arbor-tristis.
paragraphs: In humid South Asian and tropical growing belts, Night-Flowering Jasmine (Shiuli) (Nyctanthes arbor-tristis) relies on secondary terpenoid resins, foliar trichomes, and phytoalexin phenolics as front-line biochemical deterrence against herbivores and opportunistic pathogens. Prolonged monsoon waterlogging or stagnant canopy humidity can nonetheless encourage anthracnose (Colletotrichum spp.), powdery mildew, leaf-spot fungi, or root-zone Pythium.

Organic Integrated Pest Management (IPM) prioritizes preventive airflow pruning, Trichoderma-enriched compost amendments around feeder roots, and targeted cold-pressed Azadirachta indica (neem) oil sprays at dusk to suppress sap-sucking aphids, scale insects, and mealybugs without harming native pollinators.

subblocks.heading: Fungal Management
subblocks.text: Prevent overhead foliar wetness at dusk; maintain canopy aeration and copper/Trichoderma prophylaxis.

subblocks.heading: Organic Pest Control
subblocks.text: Neem kernel emulsion (3–5 ml/L) plus conservation of hoverfly and ladybird predator guilds.

sections.title: Conservation Standing & Climate Resilience
sections.subtitle: Population security, agroforestry corridors, and stress tolerance
sections.summary: Biogeographic conservation standing and climate adaptation traits of Night-Flowering Jasmine (Shiuli).
paragraphs: Across its native and naturalized distribution (South & Southeast Asia (Himalayan Foothills to Bengal & Thailand)), Night-Flowering Jasmine (Shiuli) (Nyctanthes arbor-tristis) demonstrates strong ecological plasticity across alluvial floodplains, homestead agroforestry plots, and urban biodiversity corridors. While cultivated stands remain broadly secure, landrace genetic erosion, coastal salinity shifts, and wetland drainage threaten wild ecotypes and heritage regional varieties.

Long-term resilience depends on decentralized in-situ homestead stewardship, wetland buffer conservation, and botanical garden germplasm collections preserving drought-, flood-, and salinity-tolerant alleles amid shifting monsoon regimes.

subblocks.heading: Ecological Resilience
subblocks.text: Adapted to South & Southeast Asia (Himalayan Foothills to Bengal & Thailand) thermal oscillations and seasonal hydrological extremes.

subblocks.heading: Stewardship Strategy
subblocks.text: Preserve traditional landraces, pollinator corridors, and living herbarium voucher plots.

sections.title: Horticultural Spacing, Pruning & Telemetry
sections.subtitle: Plot geometry, canopy shaping, and calibrated soil-climate meters
sections.summary: Calibrated horticultural parameters: pH 5.8 – 7.5, Full Sun / Light Afternoon Shade, and structural spacing guidance.
paragraphs: Optimal managed cultivation of Night-Flowering Jasmine (Shiuli) (Nyctanthes arbor-tristis) calibrates root-zone chemistry around pH 5.8 – 7.5 inside humus-rich fertile loam. Providing adequate crown spacing prevents humidity buildup and lets lower shoots capture uniform irradiance across full sun / light afternoon shade.

Light corrective pruning immediately after main flowering or harvest periods redirects assimilates into healthy vegetative framework, while moisture scheduling (moderate / well-drained) stabilizes root turgor without inducing hypoxia.

subblocks.text: Full Sun / Light Afternoon Shade · Moderate / Well-Drained

sections.title: Evolutionary Genetics & Adaptive Phylogeny
sections.subtitle: Lamiales clade divergence and Oleaceae genomic traits
sections.summary: Phylogenetic placement of genus Nyctanthes within order Lamiales (Eudicot (Lamiids)).
paragraphs: Modern molecular phylogenetics (APG IV) places Nyctanthes arbor-tristis inside family Oleaceae (ওলিয়াসি (বেলি-জলপাই গোত্র)), order Lamiales, clade Eudicot (Lamiids). Olive and jasmine woody climbers and trees recognized by opposite leaves and intensely fragrant, star-like white corollas rich in benzyl acetate.

Within genus Nyctanthes, specialized morphological adaptations—such as opposite simple or trifoliate leaves without stipules—reflect co-evolutionary specialization with regional pollinator guilds and abiotic habitat filters.

sections.title: Field Identification Key & Diagnostic Checks
sections.subtitle: Macro-morphological verification against look-alike taxa
sections.summary: Rapid field-sheet checklist for confirming Nyctanthes arbor-tristis (Shiuli (শিউলি)).
paragraphs: Field verification of Night-Flowering Jasmine (Shiuli) (Nyctanthes arbor-tristis) rests on recognizing key Oleaceae family markers: Opposite simple or trifoliate leaves without stipules; Nocturnal fragrance release timed for crepuscular moth pollination; Paired stamens attached inside slender tubular floral throats. Inspecting fresh leaf arrangement, stem surface texture, and reproductive architecture together eliminates confusion with sympatric congeners.
